note: Punch-list 9.1. The garments below are MPFB2's CC0 assets and are PLUMBING STAND-INS, not the shipping capsule — 9.9 authors that. They exist so dress/undress, the hide-mask rebuild and the asset gate are exercised against real skinned geometry rather than a fixture.
fragmentPaths: Relative to THIS FILE, not to the repo root. The build writes them, the runtime resolves them against the manifest's own URL, and the node selftest against its own directory — so moving the wardrobe directory moves everything in it and nothing has to be rewritten.
figureCoverage: Only g050 is declared. A garment fragment CANNOT be shared across the five figures — female_casualsuit01 drifts mean 95.145 mm / max 143.066 mm between g000 and g100, and cross-fitting puts 84.4% of the covered skin outside the cloth (research/wardrobe-system.md §3.3). Punch-list 9.4 bakes the other four and measures the fit; declaring paths to files nobody has measured would be a promise this manifest cannot keep, and GarmentManifest.fragmentUrl throws a named error for a figure a garment does not ship.

layers.name: FOUNDATION
layers.description: Bra, briefs, boxer brief, vest. Punch-list 9.8 authors these; nothing may remove them and they carry no hide mask of their own.

layers.name: BASE
layers.description: Shirt, tee, trousers, skirt, dress, one-piece suit — the layer worn directly over the foundation.

garments.name: Casual suit
garments.cloSource: ASHRAE 55-2013 Table 5.2.2.2B, additive per §5.2.2.2(c): long-sleeve dress shirt 0.25 + trousers, thin 0.15. The table has no one-piece casual suit; this is the sum of its two parts, and the sum is what the standard says to do.
garments.formalitySource: AUTHORED. research/wardrobe-system.md §6 records that no literature supports a formality ladder; the number is a design choice and is marked as one.
garments.source: MPFB2 / MakeHuman system assets, CC0 (released September 2020 by Data Collection AB, Joel Palmius, Jonas Hauquier).

garments.name: Fedora
garments.cloSource: NONE. ASHRAE 55-2013 Table 5.2.2.2B lists no headwear, and research/wardrobe-system.md §6.1 makes clo the seasonal input. A fabricated value would corrupt every ensemble sum, so this garment declares no insulation and Dresser (9.11) must treat null as 'contributes nothing', not as zero-because-measured.
garments.source: MPFB2 / MakeHuman system assets, CC0. Measured: this asset carries NO delete_verts at all, which is why hideMask is null — a hat hides nothing.

garments.name: Elegant suit
garments.cloSource: ASHRAE 55-2013 Table 5.2.2.2B, additive: long-sleeve dress shirt 0.25 + trousers, thin 0.15 + suit jacket, single-breasted, thin 0.36 would be 0.76; this asset is a dress and jacket rather than three pieces, so the sum used is dress-equivalent (shirt 0.25 + trousers 0.15) plus a thin jacket 0.36 minus the trousers it does not have. AUTHORED ARITHMETIC over table rows — flagged, because the table has no row for this garment.
garments.source: MPFB2 / MakeHuman system assets, CC0. Present because it collides with female_casualsuit01 on every slot at the same layer, which is the state MPFB attaches today with no warning — the two suits interpenetrate and both delete groups apply as a union (research §2.2). It is the manifest gate's known-bad.
